edition.title: The Hunger Games
edition.author: Suzanne Collins
edition.description: In the ruins of a place once known as North America lies the nation of Panem. Each year, its twelve districts must send one boy and one girl to compete in the Hunger Games, a fight to the death on live television.

edition.title: The Hunger Games
edition.author: Suzanne Collins
edition.description: In the ruins of a place once known as North America lies the nation of Panem. Each year, its twelve districts must send one boy and one girl to compete in the Hunger Games, a fight to the death on live television.

publicReception.summary: Readers describe a fast, tense survival story that is hard to put down, carried by a guarded, practical narrator. Many read it as a sharp comment on cruelty staged as entertainment. The main complaints are a love triangle that slows the second half, plain present-tense prose, and violence involving children that some found hard to read.

praises.text: Fast pacing that is hard to put down

complaints.text: The love triangle slows the second half
Plain, flat writing style
Violence involving children is hard to read

evidence.excerpt: In the ruins of a place once known as North America lies the nation of Panem. Each year, its twelve districts must send one boy and one girl to compete in the Hunger Games, a fight to the death on live television.
I read it in two sittings. Every chapter ends on something that makes you turn the page.
Katniss is a narrator you trust: practical, guarded, and fierce about her sister.
Fast and tense, with a sharp point about entertainment and cruelty.
The love triangle felt forced and slowed the second half for me.
Gripping, but the violence against children was hard to read at times.
The writing is plain; the present tense never stopped feeling flat.
